title: Fast and high-fidelity in situ 3D imaging protocol for stem cells and niche components for mouse organs and tissues
protocol: Rinse the bones 2 times with 10 mL PBS in 15 mL tubes to remove PFA solution.
Dry the bones with tissue; ensure they are clean and remove any redundant tissue.
Fill cryomolds with OCT until reaching the upper limit.
Position bones longitudinally close to the left side of the OCT containing cryomold, ensuring they are fully immersed and parallel to the left edge.
Move bubbles out if present during positioning.
Snap freeze filled cryomolds in liquid nitrogen using long-armed tweezers.
Touch gently with the bottom of the cryomold the surface of the LN2 in an appropriate open LN2 Dewar flask.
Wait until a bubbling sound begins, indicating proper attachment.
Allow the OCT to freeze from bottom to top, turning completely white.
When the OCT is totally frozen, drop it into the LN2.
Store the frozen and embedded tissue at −80°C for long-term preservation.
Transfer the samples to dry ice to prevent OCT melting.
Freeze the frozen block on a specimen chuck using OCT with the tissue upside down.
Shave the block with the trimming function until the bone marrow is maximally exposed.
Switch to the sectioning thickness and shave the specimen 10–20 times.
Check during shaving steps for notches caused by the bone matrix, shift blade or use a new one if needed.
Remove debris from the sample using a brush.
Cut the frozen tissue block with a razor blade from the specimen chuck.
Store shaved samples at −80°C for up to 3–4 weeks prior to immunofluorescence staining.
Place the shaved and frozen samples into a box with separating chambers filled with cold (4°C) washing buffer solution to cover the samples.
Wait until the OCT around the sample is melted in the cold (4°C) washing buffer solution.
Melt the OCT.
Take out exposed samples cautiously with tweezers.
Wash bones with washing buffer solution using a plastic bottle to remove sticky OCT.
Prepare 24-well plates for fixation and washing.
Fill one well of the 24-well plate with 2 mL of 4% PFA fixation solution for each sample.
Place bone samples into the fixation solution, ensuring the shaved surface is up and the BM does not touch the bottom.
Incubate at 18°C–25°C for 30 minutes.
Wash the samples 3× 20 min at 18°C–25°C using washing buffer solution.
Relocate samples from well to well, each containing 2 mL of washing buffer.
Place the samples in 0.2 mL PCR tubes with blocking and permeabilization buffer.
Incubate the samples at 18°C–25°C for 1 h.
Prepare a lineage antibody cocktail solution using biotinylated anti-CD41, anti-CD48, anti-CD11b, anti-B220, anti-CD5, anti-Gr-1, anti-Ter119, and anti-CD8a in antibody diluent buffer.
Incubate the solution at 4°C for 2 days.
Spin down antibody vials to remove aggregates and precipitates.
Wash the samples 3× 20 min at 18°C–25°C using washing buffer solution.
Prepare a secondary antibody solution with streptavidin (eFluor®450- or FITC-conjugated) in antibody diluent buffer.
Incubate the sample at 18°C–25°C for 2 h.
Wash the samples 3× 20 min at 18°C–25°C using washing buffer solution.
Prepare antibody solution with anti-CD150-PE at a concentration of 4 μg/mL in antibody diluent buffer.
Incubate the antibody solution at 4°C for 3 days.
Wash the samples 3 times, each time for 20 minutes, at a temperature between 18°C and 25°C using washing buffer solution.
Place bone samples in a 24-well plate with shaved surface down, adding 2 mL of storage buffer solution per well.
Store the samples at 4°C in the dark until ready for microscopy.
Drop 30 μL to 80 μL of washing and storage buffer solution into the bottom glass of a 4-well-μ-slide to prevent tissue desiccation.
Place the fluorescently labeled tissue cut-face down onto the drop in the 4-well-μ-slide, ensuring the sample surface is completely touching the glass planar.
Cover the microscope glass chamber with the associated lid.
Switch on the confocal microscope system.
Place the glass chamber on the stage of the microscope.
Use a 10× objective for preview and choose a region for setting up in the widefield mode.
Set up the acquisition settings for confocal microscopy.
Set up the channel configurations based on the excitation/emission parameters of the used fluorochromes and dyes in the staining.
Note: If available, use the auto-set-up mode with the ideal option.
Use transmitted light detection (DIC) for trabecular and cortical bone matrix detection and for structural details.
Use an image size resolution of 1024 × 1024 with bidirectional scanning (600 Hz–800 Hz) and 3–5× averaging.
Switch to a 20× objective and confocal live mode.
Optimize the detector parameters gain, laser power etc. by negative controls and/or by a software over-saturation option.
Avoid long-lasting laser exposure of the region of interest (ROI) to prevent photobleaching of sensitive types of labeled antibodies.
Scan for a ROI using 10× objective in the widefield mode.
Switch back to a 20× objective and confocal live mode.
Set up the z-stack configurations.
Set up the lower focal plane scanning limit.
Set up the upper focal plane scanning limit.
Use a step size between 1.0 μm to 3.5 μm for z-stack tile scanning.
Start the scanning procedure for 3D imaging.
Save your z-stack data after scanning.
Import raw images into Volocity software.
Go to the “File” menu and select “New Library…”.
Name the library and choose a destination for storage.
Drag the raw image or folder with images into the “Library” view on the left side of the screen.
Select the image from the “Library” view for 3D visualization.
Change the display option to “3D Opacity” in the drop-down menu at the top of the screen.
Use the tools at the top of the window to change actions for rotating and zooming for a required 3D view.
Optimize the brightness for individual channels on the channel control view.
Set the density for individual channels on the channel control view.
Adjust the black level for individual channels on the channel control view.
Choose the proper rendering mode from the channel control view.
Select “Show Scale” from the “Image” menu to display a scale bar.
Select “Show Orientation” from the “Display” menu to show XYZ-orientation.
Go to the “Image” menu and select “Capture Snapshot…” to create an image illustration.
Export the snapshot of the 3D visualization using the “File” menu.
